name: build_proposal_two_way_bike_lane
notes: apply_osm_parking(louellen_st_west, right): 5.7 ft hatched - too narrow for a stall
apply_osm_parking(louellen_st_west, left): 8 ft stalls + 0.6 ft hatched to the kerb - no restriction tagged

AddTwoWayBikeLane(w_broad_st_northeast, left): 8 ft two-way lane, 3 ft buffer. Spends 11.82 ft of this leg's 31.96 ft between kerbs, leaving two 10.07 ft travel lanes with the centreline shifted 7.23 ft toward the right kerb - under the 11 ft target by 0.93 ft, which is this leg's width rather than a choice, so the travel way is split equally. The NJDOT alignment does not move; every station and crossing frame is measured from it as before. NOTE: NJDOT's Bicycle Compatible Roadways and Bikeways (1996) calls a two-way bike lane on one side of the roadway 'unacceptable'; that guidance predates separated bikeways and MUTCD 11th ed. 9E.06 now marks them, but the departure has to be argued, not assumed - see STANDARDS.md 4.

AddBikeLaneBollards(w_broad_st_northeast, left): flex-post delineators at 8 ft in the 3 ft buffer between the travel lane and the bike lane - the traffic side, which is the side that needs protecting.

props.source: real (OSM node 14068526388, where a crossing way meets barrier=kerb way 1546755070 tagged tactile_paving=yes): the surveyed curb ramp. One pad per attach node, so two crossings meeting at one node render as the single shared ramp they are. Approximation: pad size is a standard one.
real (OSM emergency=fire_hydrant node): surveyed position.
